1: //! stylus — the owned stylus/tablet input crate.
2: //!
3: //! The must-own layer (docs/research/03 §2): winit has no X11 pen events,
4: //! no Wintab, and its 0.31 pen events are still beta. Umber therefore owns
5: //! a dual-path input layer:
6: //!   - Windows: Windows Ink (WM_POINTER) AND Wintab32 polling (runtime
7: //!     switch; external tablets commonly run Wintab).
8: //!   - Linux: Wayland zwp_tablet_unstable_v2 + X11 XI2 valuator axes.
9: //!
10: //! Wave 1 scope: the backend-agnostic event vocabulary + platform
11: //! dispatch skeleton. Concrete backend code is feature-gated and lands
12: //! incrementally (Windows Ink first per SPEC Wave 1).
13: 
14: use std::fmt;
15: 
16: #[cfg(all(windows, feature = "winink"))]
17: pub mod winink;
18: 
19: /// A raw tablet event, normalized across backends.
20: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
21: pub enum TabletEvent {
22:     /// Pen entered proximity.
23:     ProximityIn { time_ns: u64 },
24:     /// Pen left proximity.
25:     ProximityOut { time_ns: u64 },
26:     /// Position/pressure/tilt update.
27:     Motion {
28:         pos: [f32; 2],
29:         pressure: f32,
30:         tilt: Option<[f32; 2]>,

32:     },

37:         button: u8,

39:         time_ns: u64,
40:     },
41: }

43: /// Which platform input path produced an event (diagnostics + tests).
44: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
45: pub enum InputSource {
46:     WindowsInk,
47:     Wintab,
48:     WaylandTablet,
49:     X11Xinput2,
50:     MouseFallback,
51: }
52: 
53: impl fmt::Display for InputSource {

1: //! The 3D viewport: owns the orbit camera and the GPU-resident mesh, and
2: //! paints into the dock's `Panel::Viewport` tab each frame.
3: //!
4: //! Never touches a `wgpu` type by name — every value it holds or passes to
5: //! `umber_gpu` is opaque to this crate (received from or handed to
6: //! `umber_gpu`'s API), per the architecture rule that GPU objects stay
7: //! behind `umber-gpu`.
8: //!
9: //! CORE-LOOP follow-up (the strategy-review disposition's first core-loop
10: //! kill: viewport texture binding; the GPU side —
11: //! `MeshBuffers::set_base_color_texture` / `clear_base_color_texture` —
12: //! landed first and waited uncallable). Each frame with a mesh loaded, the
13: //! paint session's ACTIVE tile is bound as the mesh pass's base-color
14: //! texture just before the draw callback is built, so the stroke you paint
15: //! is the stroke you see lit in 3D. Judgment calls, all v1:
16: //!
17: //! * One tile bound at a time — the active tile
18: //!   (`PaintState::active_tile` + `tile_target`), not a hardcoded 1001.
19: //!   Single-tile sessions always have the active tile at 1001, so their
20: //!   behavior is unchanged; multi-tile meshes show the tile under the last
21: //!   pointer. The tile-pool atlas + page-table indirection (every tile at
22: //!   once) is the architecture doc's named later slice.
23: //! * The tile select is `PaintParams::for_udim` (the real constructor —
24: //!   there is no `for_tile(tile, size)`); no target size enters the bind
25: //!   because the shader samples in UV space and the texel density lives in
26: //!   `PaintState`.
27: //! * Re-bound EVERY frame while paint is present: a `Resize` command
28: //!   replaces the tile's texture object, so a params-equality skip would
29: //!   keep sampling the evicted texture. The matching clear is skipped once
30: //!   already cleared (flags == 0 holds no view — provably identical).
31: //! * The bind sits before the route match, so the Direct and PostFx arms
32: //!   both see paint (the PostFx path reuses the mesh's own callback).
33: //! * No paint session (or a session tile with no target yet) clears back
34: //!   to the constant arm — pixel-identical to a mesh that never bound
35: //!   paint, and the mesh-less empty-state hero path is untouched (it binds
36: //!   nothing at all).

62: /// An eyedropper sample (C1 worklist #10): the sRGBA bytes the viewport
63: /// read from the paint target at the clicked UV, one per Pick click.
64: /// Carried to the shell so it can set the brush color (and later: the
65: /// alpha, masks, anything color-keyed) from what the artist actually
66: /// sees on the mesh.
67: pub struct PickSample(pub [u8; 4]);

69: /// One LINEAR u8 texel component to its sRGB byte (the eyedropper's
70: /// per-texel conversion; matches umber-color's private `linear_to_srgb`

72: fn linear_to_srgb_byte(linear: u8) -> u8 {

235:                         // sample is the follow-up when the picker meets the
236:                         // display chain).

240:                                 as u32;
241:                             let y = ((uv[1].clamp(0.0, 1.0)) * (image.height as f32 - 1.0)).round()
242:                                 as u32;
243:                             let i = (y * image.width + x) as usize * 4;
244:                             if i + 3 < image.data.len() {
245:                                 let srgba = [
246:                                     linear_to_srgb_byte(image.data[i]),
247:                                     linear_to_srgb_byte(image.data[i + 1]),
248:                                     linear_to_srgb_byte(image.data[i + 2]),
249:                                     image.data[i + 3],
250:                                 ];

252:                             }
253:                         }

255:                 }

257:         }

262:             && self.mesh_data.is_some()

264:                 .as_ref()
265:                 .is_some_and(|p| p.projection().viewport_paints());

274:                 // per-event force feeds the stroke. The source is the RAW
275:                 // `Event::Touch` stream, NOT `multi_touch()`: the gesture
276:                 // aggregate returns `None` below two active touches
277:                 // (egui's own contract — "returns None for single-touch
278:                 // gestures"), so a single pen contact never carried force
279:                 // through it and painted at a constant 1.0 (the cross-review
280:                 // finding on f867215, receipt 2026-10-12-pressure-kill-
281:                 // cross-review-receipt.md). `Event::Touch` carries

283:                 // in 0..=1; `None`/0.0 maps to 1.0 — a mouse drag (no touch
284:                 // events at all) and a platform that cannot measure force
285:                 // both paint at full pressure, never a ghost-faint stroke.
286:                 // V1 takes the frame's LAST touch event's force (the
287:                 // single-pen case; per-touch-id tracking rides with the
288:                 // stylus-crate backends — Windows Ink, XI2 — the named
289:                 // follow-up for tilt, proximity, eraser).

291:                     .input(|i| {
292:                         let mut force: Option<f32> = None;
293:                         for event in &i.events {
294:                             if let egui::Event::Touch {
295:                                 phase: egui::TouchPhase::Start | egui::TouchPhase::Move,
296:                                 pos,
297:                                 force: f,
298:                                 ..
299:                             } = event
300:                             {
301:                                 // Only the touch stream inside this viewport
302:                                 // feeds the stroke: a second finger landing on
303:                                 // a panel mid-stroke must not override the
304:                                 // pen's force for the frame.
305:                                 if rect.contains(*pos) {
306:                                     force = *f;
307:                                 }
308:                             }
309:                         }
310:                         force

414:     /// Casts a ray through the pointer position and returns the mesh UV
415:     /// at the nearest hit (or `None` on miss). NDC Y matches the
416:     /// directx/wgpu convention (up = +1). The NDC→world unprojection is
417:     /// the shared [`umber_gpu::world_from_ndc`] helper (deduped with the
418:     /// ground grid's test math — same function, not a copy).
419:     fn pick_uv(
420:         &self,
421:         rect: egui::Rect,
422:         mesh: &umber_mesh::MeshData,
423:         pos: egui::Pos2,
424:     ) -> Option<[f32; 2]> {
425:         let aspect = rect.width() / rect.height();
426:         let ndc_x = (pos.x - rect.left()) / rect.width() * 2.0 - 1.0;
427:         let ndc_y = 1.0 - (pos.y - rect.top()) / rect.height() * 2.0;
428:         let view_proj = self.camera.view_proj(aspect);
429:         let inv = view_proj.inverse();
430:         // Unproject the near (z=0) and far (z=1) NDC points (directx
431:         // depth convention) to build the ray.
432:         let near = umber_gpu::world_from_ndc(inv, glam::Vec4::new(ndc_x, ndc_y, 0.0, 1.0));
433:         let far = umber_gpu::world_from_ndc(inv, glam::Vec4::new(ndc_x, ndc_y, 1.0, 1.0));
434:         let dir = far - near;
435:         let hit = umber_mesh::ray_intersect(mesh, self.camera.eye(), dir)?;

469: /// UV derivation: [`PaintParams::for_udim`] subtracts the tile origin
470: /// (`(tile - 1001) % 10`, `(tile - 1001) / 10`) at scale 1 — the exact
471: /// inverse of [`crate::paint_state`] tile-local mapping (its `local_texel`
472: /// subtracts the same offsets before the V-flipped texel map), so the
473: /// shader's `(uv - offset) * scale` lands on the bound tile's own texels.
474: fn bind_paint_target(
475:     gpu: &GpuContext,
476:     mesh: &mut MeshBuffers,
477:     paint: Option<&crate::paint_state::PaintState>,
478: ) {
479:     let Some(paint) = paint else {

482:         if mesh.paint_params().flags != 0 {

1: //! UI string catalogs (`docs/specs/i18n-design.md`): Fluent bundles over
2: //! `assets/i18n/<locale>.ftl`, a per-thread current locale, and the
3: //! [`tr`] / [`tr_args`] lookups every migrated UI string goes through.
4: //!
5: //! # Keys
6: //!
7: //! The code calls dotted keys (`group.name`). Fluent message ids cannot
8: //! contain dots, so a dotted key resolves to message `group`, attribute
9: //! `.name` (see `en-US.ftl`); an undotted key resolves to a message value.
10: //!
11: //! # Fallback (never a panic, never a blank)
12: //!
13: //! A lookup tries the current locale's bundle, then [`FALLBACK_LOCALE`],
14: //! then returns the key itself. Debug builds log each missing key once.
15: //! Only the top surface (menus, panel titles, primary buttons, two status
16: //! phrases) is migrated in v1; the long tail stays hardcoded and moves to
17: //! keys as it is touched. The completeness test below checks that every
18: //! key the source calls exists in en-US.
19: //!
20: //! # Where catalogs come from ([`I18n::load_all`])
21: //!
22: //! 1. The built-in catalogs, embedded at compile time: the installers do
23: //!    not ship `assets/`, so en-US and pt-BR always work.
24: //! 2. Every `*.ftl` in the discovered catalog dirs ([`catalog_dirs`]),
25: //!    the file stem naming the locale. A discovered file replaces the
26: //!    built-in bundle for its locale, so dev edits show without a rebuild
27: //!    and a new `<locale>.ftl` is a new picker entry.
28: //!
29: //! # The locale choice
30: //!
31: //! At startup: the persisted preference ([`locale_pref_path`]), else the
32: //! system locale, else en-US. The system locale is env-based in v1 —
33: //! `LC_ALL`, then `LC_MESSAGES`, then `LANG` (POSIX precedence) — because
34: //! egui exposes no OS-locale query. On Windows those vars are usually
35: //! unset, so the app starts in en-US until a language is picked; an OS
36: //! query there is the named follow-up.
37: //!
38: //! The preference is a one-line file next to the per-user brushes and
39: //! plugins dirs (`$XDG_DATA_HOME/umber/locale`, `%APPDATA%\umber\locale`).
40: //! It is an app preference, not a document property, so it does not live
41: //! with `DisplaySettings` in the `.umber` project.
42: //!
43: //! # Threading
44: //!
45: //! Fluent's default bundle is not `Sync`, so the current catalog is a
46: //! thread-local: the UI thread (where `main` installs it) is the only
47: //! one that renders strings. Any other thread lazily gets the built-in
48: //! catalogs in en-US — which is also what keeps tests deterministic
49: //! regardless of the machine's `LANG`.

51: use std::cell::RefCell;
52: use std::collections::{HashMap, HashSet};
53: use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
54: 
55: use fluent::{FluentArgs, FluentBundle, FluentResource, FluentValue};
56: 
57: /// The source-of-truth locale and the last resort before the bare key.
58: pub const FALLBACK_LOCALE: &str = "en-US";
59: 
60: /// The catalogs compiled into the binary.
61: const BUILTIN: &[(&str, &str)] = &[
62:     ("en-US", include_str!("../../../assets/i18n/en-US.ftl")),
63:     ("pt-BR", include_str!("../../../assets/i18n/pt-BR.ftl")),
64: ];

66: /// The repo-relative catalog dir (correct when CWD is the repo root).
67: pub const CATALOG_DIR: &str = "assets/i18n";

69: /// The loaded catalogs plus the current locale.
70: pub struct I18n {
71:     locale: String,
72:     bundles: HashMap<String, FluentBundle<FluentResource>>,
73:     /// Keys already warned about (debug builds), so a missing key logs
74:     /// once instead of every frame.
75:     warned: RefCell<HashSet<String>>,
76: }

78: impl I18n {
79:     /// The built-in catalogs only, in en-US.
80:     pub fn builtin() -> Self {
81:         Self::from_sources(BUILTIN)
82:     }
83: 
84:     /// The built-in catalogs overlaid with every `*.ftl` under
85:     /// [`catalog_dirs`], in en-US (see the module docs).
86:     pub fn load_all() -> Self {
87:         let mut i18n = Self::builtin();
88:         for dir in catalog_dirs() {
89:             i18n.load_dir(&dir);
90:         }
91:         i18n
92:     }

94:     /// Bundles from in-memory `(locale, ftl source)` pairs, in en-US.
95:     pub fn from_sources(sources: &[(&str, &str)]) -> Self {
96:         let mut i18n = Self {
97:             locale: FALLBACK_LOCALE.to_owned(),
98:             bundles: HashMap::new(),
99:             warned: RefCell::new(HashSet::new()),
100:         };
101:         for (locale, source) in sources {
102:             i18n.add_catalog(locale, source);
103:         }
104:         i18n
105:     }

107:     /// Adds (or replaces) `locale`'s bundle from Fluent source. Syntax
108:     /// errors keep the entries that did parse and log the rest; an
109:     /// unparseable locale tag is skipped with a warning.
110:     pub fn add_catalog(&mut self, locale: &str, source: &str) {
111:         let resource = match FluentResource::try_new(source.to_owned()) {
112:             Ok(res) => res,
113:             Err((res, errors)) => {
114:                 log::warn!("i18n: {locale}.ftl has syntax errors: {errors:?}");
115:                 res
116:             }
117:         };
118:         let mut bundle = match locale.parse() {
119:             Ok(langid) => FluentBundle::new(vec![langid]),
120:             Err(err) => {
121:                 log::warn!("i18n: skipping catalog with bad locale tag {locale:?}: {err}");
122:                 return;
123:             }
124:         };
125:         // No U+2068/U+2069 isolation marks around placeables: egui draws
126:         // them as boxes, and none of our args are bidi-sensitive.
127:         bundle.set_use_isolating(false);
128:         if let Err(errors) = bundle.add_resource(resource) {
129:             log::warn!("i18n: {locale}.ftl has duplicate entries: {errors:?}");
130:         }

132:     }

134:     /// Loads every direct-child `*.ftl` in `dir` (file stem = locale).
135:     /// A missing/unreadable dir or file is a silent skip.
136:     pub fn load_dir(&mut self, dir: &Path) {
137:         let Ok(entries) = std::fs::read_dir(dir) else {
138:             return;
139:         };

141:             .filter_map(|e| e.ok().map(|e| e.path()))
142:             .filter(|p| p.extension().is_some_and(|ext| ext == "ftl"))
143:             .collect();
144:         paths.sort();
145:         for path in paths {
146:             let (Some(stem), Ok(source)) = (
147:                 path.file_stem().and_then(|s| s.to_str()),
148:                 std::fs::read_to_string(&path),
149:             ) else {
150:                 continue;
151:             };
152:             self.add_catalog(stem, &source);
153:         }
154:     }

163:         let mut tags: Vec<String> = self.bundles.keys().cloned().collect();
164:         tags.sort();
165:         tags
166:     }

168:     /// Switches to `wanted` (negotiated: see [`Self::negotiate`]).
169:     /// Returns the locale now active; an unavailable request leaves the
170:     /// current locale unchanged.
171:     pub fn set_locale(&mut self, wanted: &str) -> &str {
172:         if let Some(tag) = self.negotiate(wanted) {

175:         &self.locale

178:     /// The loaded locale best matching `wanted`: an exact tag match
179:     /// (case-insensitive), else the first loaded locale with the same
180:     /// language (`pt` or `pt-PT` → `pt-BR`), else `None`.
181:     pub fn negotiate(&self, wanted: &str) -> Option<String> {
182:         let tags = self.locales();
183:         if let Some(tag) = tags.iter().find(|t| t.eq_ignore_ascii_case(wanted)) {
184:             return Some(tag.clone());
185:         }
186:         let language = |t: &str| t.split('-').next().unwrap_or("").to_ascii_lowercase();
187:         let want = language(wanted);
188:         tags.into_iter()
189:             .find(|t| !want.is_empty() && language(t) == want)
190:     }

194:     pub fn choose_startup_locale(&mut self, pref: Option<&str>, system: Option<&str>) {
195:         let chosen = [pref, system]

197:             .flatten()
198:             .find_map(|wanted| self.negotiate(wanted))
199:             .unwrap_or_else(|| FALLBACK_LOCALE.to_owned());
200:         self.locale = chosen;
201:     }

212:     pub fn lookup(&self, key: &str, args: Option<&FluentArgs>) -> String {
213:         for locale in [self.locale.as_str(), FALLBACK_LOCALE] {
214:             if let Some(text) = self
215:                 .bundles
216:                 .get(locale)
217:                 .and_then(|bundle| format_in(bundle, key, args))
218:             {

221:         }

223:             log::warn!("i18n: missing key {key:?} (locale {})", self.locale);
224:         }

226:     }

229: /// Formats `key` (dotted = message + attribute) from one bundle; `None`
230: /// when the message, attribute or value is absent.
231: fn format_in(
232:     bundle: &FluentBundle<FluentResource>,
233:     key: &str,
234:     args: Option<&FluentArgs>,
235: ) -> Option<String> {
236:     let (id, attribute) = match key.split_once('.') {
237:         Some((id, attr)) => (id, Some(attr)),
238:         None => (key, None),
239:     };
240:     let message = bundle.get_message(id)?;
241:     let pattern = match attribute {
242:         Some(attr) => message.get_attribute(attr)?.value(),
243:         None => message.value()?,
244:     };
245:     let mut errors = Vec::new();
246:     let text = bundle.format_pattern(pattern, args, &mut errors);
247:     if !errors.is_empty() {
248:         log::warn!("i18n: formatting {key:?}: {errors:?}");
249:     }
250:     Some(text.into_owned())
251: }

1: //! umber-app library surface — the paint session for integration tests.
2: //!
3: //! The desktop shell is a binary (`main.rs`); integration tests under
4: //! `tests/` can only link against a library target, so this crate exposes
5: //! the two modules the Gate-0 journey test drives:
6: //!
7: //! * [`paint_state`]: the live paint session (`PaintState` — 4K target,
8: //!   pressure entry points, stroke undo, the fill-upload path the project
9: //!   open path restores through).
10: //! * [`retouch`]: the session's undo-command types (re-exported for the
11: //!   `paint_state` signatures that name them).
12: //!
13: //! Judgment calls (v1 boundaries):
14: //!
15: //! * This surface is additive: `main.rs` keeps its own `mod paint_state;`
16: //!   / `mod retouch;` declarations (same files, compiled once per crate —
17: //!   legal, and zero risk to the shell). Nothing is moved or re-wired.
18: //! * Only what the journey test needs is reachable: `paint_state`'s
19: //!   remaining `pub(crate)` test hooks (`set_brush_params`, `read_tile`,
20: //!   …) stay crate-private to each crate. The widened seams are
21: //!   [`paint_state::PaintState::publish_fill`] and
22: //!   [`paint_state::PaintState::set_brush_color`] (`pub(crate)` → `pub`):
23: //!   the project open path restores sidecar PNGs through the former, and
24: //!   the journey test paints its color-identifiable stroke through the
25: //!   latter — so a save/reopen leg that cannot restore, or a paint leg
26: //!   that cannot name its color, is not Gate 0.
27: //! * The eframe shell itself (`save_project` / `open_project`'s dialogs
28: //!   and the `project.json` commit) stays shell-only; the journey test
29: //!   replicates their sidecar file round-trip through the same helpers
30: //!   (`umber_export::png::{write_png, read_png_rgba8}`) and the same
31: //!   session calls, and names that boundary in its own module docs.
32: 
33: pub mod paint_state;
34: pub mod retouch;

1: //! The bottom status bar (GUI roadmap Phase 0b,
2: //! docs/specs/gui-audit-and-roadmap.md Part 3): cursor UV | UDIM tile | fps.
3: //!
4: //! The format functions are pure (no `tr()`, no egui) and pinned by the
5: //! tests below. [`show`] only lays them out next to localized labels.
6: //!
7: //! # Judgment calls
8: //!
9: //! - **Cursor UV comes from the 2D UV view's hover, not the 3D viewport.**
10: //!   The UV view maps the pointer to UV with one division
11: //!   (`paint_state::uv_from_pointer`). A 3D hover readout would need a
12: //!   per-move ray cast, and `umber_mesh::ray_intersect` is a brute-force
13: //!   loop over every triangle (no BVH). Per-hover cost on a production
14: //!   mesh is not v1 material. The 3D readout lands with the
15: //!   paint-cursor layer (roadmap Phase 2 item 4), which needs the same
16: //!   hover pick anyway.
17: //! - **The UV is absolute (UDIM space).** The UV view draws one tile's
18: //!   0..1 square: the paint session's active tile (`PaintState::
19: //!   active_tile`). The readout adds that tile's grid origin, so it reads
20: //!   the same coordinate the mesh stores (tile 1012, local (0.5, 0.25) →
21: //!   (1.500, 1.250)).
22: //! - **The tile is the active paint tile**, shown even when the pointer is
23: //!   off the UV view. Without a paint session there is no tile, and it
24: //!   reads "—".
25: //! - **fps is `1 / stable_dt`.** egui repaints reactively (on input or a
26: //!   requested repaint), so this is the rate while frames are being
27: //!   drawn, not a free-running counter. The bar never requests continuous
28: //!   repaints to make the number "live": that would burn a core while the
29: //!   app idles.
30: //! - **One frame stale by construction.** The bar is a bottom panel, so it
31: //!   draws before the dock (egui lays panels out first). It shows the hover
32: //!   the UV view recorded last frame. main.rs requests one extra repaint
33: //!   when the hover changed, so the bar catches up within a frame.
34: //! - **GPU memory is omitted.** wgpu has no portable VRAM query. The
35: //!   allocator report is backend-specific and not exposed through
36: //!   `umber-gpu`, and this crate never names wgpu types. Summing our own
37: //!   texture sizes would be a lower bound passed off as a reading. It
38: //!   stays off the bar until `umber-gpu` can report a real number.
39: 
40: use egui::{RichText, Ui};
41: use umber_gui::theme;
42: 
43: use crate::i18n::tr;
44: 
45: /// What the bar shows this frame.
46: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Default)]
47: pub struct StatusSnapshot {
48:     /// The absolute (UDIM-space) UV under the cursor, if it is over the
49:     /// UV view's square.
50:     pub cursor_uv: Option<[f32; 2]>,
51:     /// The active paint tile.
52:     pub tile: Option<u16>,
53:     /// `egui::InputState::stable_dt`, seconds.
54:     pub frame_dt: f32,
55: }
56: 
57: /// The placeholder for a value that has no reading.
58: pub const NO_VALUE: &str = "—";
59: 
60: /// The grid origin `(u, v)` of a UDIM tile (`1001 + u + 10 v`). Tiles
61: /// below 1001 clamp to the first tile, like `umber_mesh::tile_of_uv`.
62: pub fn tile_origin(tile: u16) -> [f32; 2] {
63:     let index = tile.saturating_sub(umber_mesh::FIRST_TILE);
64:     [f32::from(index % 10), f32::from(index / 10)]
65: }
66: 
67: /// The absolute UV of a tile-local UV in `tile`.
68: pub fn absolute_uv(tile: u16, local: [f32; 2]) -> [f32; 2] {
69:     let [u0, v0] = tile_origin(tile);
70:     [u0 + local[0], v0 + local[1]]
71: }
72: 
73: /// `"u, v"` at 3 decimals, or [`NO_VALUE`] for no reading or a
74: /// non-finite component. Three decimals resolve a texel at 1K, and the
75: /// fixed width keeps the bar from jittering.
76: pub fn format_uv(uv: Option<[f32; 2]>) -> String {
77:     match uv {
78:         Some([u, v]) if u.is_finite() && v.is_finite() => format!("{u:.3}, {v:.3}"),
79:         _ => NO_VALUE.to_owned(),
80:     }
81: }
82: 
83: /// The tile number, or [`NO_VALUE`].
84: pub fn format_tile(tile: Option<u16>) -> String {
85:     tile.map_or_else(|| NO_VALUE.to_owned(), |t| t.to_string())
86: }
87: 
88: /// Frames per second from a frame delta. `None` for a zero, negative or
89: /// non-finite delta (the first frame, or a clock hiccup).
90: pub fn fps_from_dt(dt: f32) -> Option<f32> {
91:     if !dt.is_finite() || dt <= 0.0 {
92:         return None;
93:     }
94:     Some(1.0 / dt)
95: }
96: 
97: /// Whole frames per second, or [`NO_VALUE`].
98: pub fn format_fps(dt: f32) -> String {
99:     fps_from_dt(dt).map_or_else(|| NO_VALUE.to_owned(), |fps| format!("{fps:.0}"))
100: }
101: 
102: /// Draws the bar into `ui`.
103: pub fn show(ui: &mut Ui, status: &StatusSnapshot) {
104:     ui.set_style(theme::umber_style(theme::Density::Compact));
105:     let label = |text: String| {
106:         RichText::new(text)
107:             .size(theme::TEXT_STATUS)
108:             .color(theme::muted())
109:     };
110:     let value = |text: String| {
111:         RichText::new(text)
112:             .size(theme::TEXT_STATUS)
113:             .monospace()
114:             .color(theme::text())
115:     };
116:     ui.horizontal(|ui| {
117:         ui.label(label(tr("status.uv")));
118:         ui.label(value(format_uv(status.cursor_uv)));
119:         ui.separator();
120:         ui.label(label(tr("status.tile")));
121:         ui.label(value(format_tile(status.tile)));
122:         ui.with_layout(egui::Layout::right_to_left(egui::Align::Center), |ui| {
123:             ui.label(label(tr("status.fps")));
124:             ui.label(value(format_fps(status.frame_dt)));
125:         });
126:     });
127: }
128: 
129: #[cfg(test)]
130: mod tests {
131:     use super::*;
132: 
133:     #[test]
134:     fn tile_origins_follow_the_udim_formula() {
135:         assert_eq!(tile_origin(1001), [0.0, 0.0]);
136:         assert_eq!(tile_origin(1002), [1.0, 0.0]);
137:         assert_eq!(tile_origin(1010), [9.0, 0.0]);
138:         assert_eq!(tile_origin(1011), [0.0, 1.0]);
139:         assert_eq!(tile_origin(1012), [1.0, 1.0]);
140:         assert_eq!(tile_origin(1100), [9.0, 9.0]);
141:         // Below the grid: clamps to the first tile.
142:         assert_eq!(tile_origin(0), [0.0, 0.0]);
143:     }
144: 
145:     #[test]
146:     fn absolute_uv_round_trips_through_tile_of_uv() {
147:         assert_eq!(absolute_uv(1012, [0.5, 0.25]), [1.5, 1.25]);
148:         assert_eq!(absolute_uv(1001, [0.5, 0.25]), [0.5, 0.25]);
149:         for tile in [1001u16, 1002, 1010, 1011, 1055, 1100] {
150:             let uv = absolute_uv(tile, [0.5, 0.5]);
151:             assert_eq!(umber_mesh::tile_of_uv(uv), tile, "tile {tile}");
152:         }
153:     }
154: 
155:     #[test]
156:     fn uv_formats_at_three_decimals() {
157:         assert_eq!(format_uv(Some([0.5, 0.25])), "0.500, 0.250");
158:         assert_eq!(format_uv(Some([1.5, 1.25])), "1.500, 1.250");
159:         // Rounds to nearest at the third decimal, carrying into the units.
160:         assert_eq!(format_uv(Some([0.12345, 0.9996])), "0.123, 1.000");
161:         assert_eq!(format_uv(None), "—");
162:         assert_eq!(format_uv(Some([f32::NAN, 0.5])), "—");
163:         assert_eq!(format_uv(Some([0.5, f32::INFINITY])), "—");
164:     }
165: 
166:     #[test]
167:     fn tile_formats_or_dashes() {
168:         assert_eq!(format_tile(Some(1001)), "1001");
169:         assert_eq!(format_tile(Some(1100)), "1100");
170:         assert_eq!(format_tile(None), "—");
171:     }
172: 
173:     #[test]
174:     fn fps_is_the_reciprocal_of_a_positive_finite_dt() {
175:         assert_eq!(fps_from_dt(0.5), Some(2.0));
176:         assert_eq!(fps_from_dt(0.25), Some(4.0));
177:         assert_eq!(fps_from_dt(0.0), None);
178:         assert_eq!(fps_from_dt(-0.016), None);
179:         assert_eq!(fps_from_dt(f32::NAN), None);
180:         assert_eq!(fps_from_dt(f32::INFINITY), None);
181:     }
182: 
183:     #[test]
184:     fn fps_formats_whole_frames() {
185:         assert_eq!(format_fps(0.5), "2");
186:         assert_eq!(format_fps(0.25), "4");
187:         // f32(1/60) and f32(1/144) aren't exact; their reciprocals land
188:         // within 1e-4 of the whole number, which `.0` rounds onto.
189:         assert_eq!(format_fps(1.0 / 60.0), "60");
190:         assert_eq!(format_fps(1.0 / 144.0), "144");
191:         assert_eq!(format_fps(0.3), "3");
192:         assert_eq!(format_fps(0.0), "—");
193:     }
194: }

92: fn map_simple_message(msg: u32, time_ns: u64) -> Option<TabletEvent> {

95:         WM_POINTERLEAVE => Some(TabletEvent::ProximityOut { time_ns }),

100:         WM_POINTERUP => Some(TabletEvent::Contact {
101:             down: false,

103:         }),

108: /// Maps a `WM_POINTERUPDATE` message plus its `POINTER_PEN_INFO` payload to
109: /// a [`TabletEvent::Motion`]. Tilt is only reported when the device marks
110: /// both tilt axes valid in `penMask` — untilt-capable digitizers leave
111: /// `tiltX`/`tiltY` at a meaningless zero.
112: fn map_pen_message(msg: u32, pen: &POINTER_PEN_INFO, time_ns: u64) -> Option<TabletEvent> {
113:     if msg != WM_POINTERUPDATE {
114:         return None;
115:     }
116: 
117:     let tilt_valid = PEN_MASK_TILT_X | PEN_MASK_TILT_Y;
118:     let tilt =
119:         (pen.penMask & tilt_valid == tilt_valid).then(|| [pen.tiltX as f32, pen.tiltY as f32]);

121:     Some(TabletEvent::Motion {
122:         pos: [
123:             pen.pointerInfo.ptPixelLocation.x as f32,
124:             pen.pointerInfo.ptPixelLocation.y as f32,
125:         ],
126:         pressure: normalize_pressure(pen.pressure),
127:         tilt,
128:         time_ns,

135: /// out-of-range [`TabletEvent::Motion::pressure`].
136: fn normalize_pressure(pressure: u32) -> f32 {
137:     (pressure as f32 / MAX_PRESSURE).clamp(0.0, 1.0)
